missing.why: Gives Base Mana Regen, not Mana; players mix up the two. Rule-correct out; no fix needed.
Long-time mana item (mana restore on hit, old Mana stat); players still name it. Current stats have no Mana, so Rule-correct out.
Spellblade items (Sheen, Lich Bane) once had Mana; veterans may try them. Rule-correct out.

disputable.why: Transformed from Manamune, not bought directly; some players will say it isn't a shop item. It has Mana in its stats, so it is in.
Transformed from Archangel's Staff; same argument as Muramana.
Transformed from Winter's Approach; same argument as Muramana.
Mostly thought of as an armor component; its Mana surprises players, but it is in.

wording.why: 'Gives Mana' could be read to include Mana Regen (Faerie Charm, Forbidden Idol) or mana restore effects. The Rule means the Mana stat only.
wording.suggestion: Name an item with Mana in its stats

aliases.why: Its name for several seasons before being renamed back.

fun.why: Tear, Manamune, Archangel's and Sapphire Crystal come instantly, and the Tear upgrades plus Frozen Heart, Luden's and Rod of Ages give most players four or five. Only 19 answers, and newer components (Actualizer, Whispering Circlet, Diadem of Songs) make a full set hard, but the set is narrow and leans on one item family.
